t: How much does it raise breast cancer risk?
key: Ask two questions: is the epithelium proliferating, and are the proliferating cells atypical? No proliferation means no added risk, proliferation alone adds a little, and atypia raises risk about fourfold to fivefold.
items: Fluid-filled cysts are part of nonproliferative fibrocystic change and leave the epithelium unchanged.
Cyst-lining cells that turn large, pink and snouted are a metaplasia, not a proliferation, so risk is unchanged.
Scarring after cyst rupture changes the stroma, not the epithelium, so it carries no added risk.
Dilated ducts with plasma cells and thick secretions are an inflammatory change without epithelial proliferation.
A fibroadenoma without complex features is a benign stromal tumor that does not raise later cancer risk.
Injured fat with calcium soaps can mimic cancer on imaging but is a healing response, not a risk marker.
Extra layers of mixed, streaming cells fill the duct, a proliferation without atypia that adds slight risk.
Increased, compressed acini with intact myoepithelium are proliferative without atypia and add slight risk.
A papillary proliferation in a large duct counts as proliferative disease without atypia.
A monotonous, clonal proliferation resembling low-grade carcinoma in situ raises risk about fourfold to fivefold.
Uniform, loosely cohesive cells partly filling acini carry the same moderate risk as ductal atypia.
Monotonous cells partly filling a duct
Evenly spaced, identical cells that do not fill the whole duct describe atypical hyperplasia, not carcinoma in situ.
